question: Who among the following was the first principal of the Bengal National College started in 1906?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurobindo Ghose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aurobindo Ghose was appointed as the first principal of the Bengal National College in 1906.
 
• The Bengal National College was part of the national education movement, which sought to promote Indian culture and education independent of British influence.
 
• Aurobindo Ghose was a prominent Indian nationalist, freedom fighter, philosopher, yogi, and poet.
 
• Under his leadership, the college aimed to provide an education that would inspire Indian youth to contribute to the freedom struggle.
 
• Aurobindo's tenure at the college marked the beginning of his active involvement in the Indian freedom movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bengal National College**

 
 
• Founded in 1906 as part of the Swadeshi movement, aiming to promote Indian education and self-reliance.
 
• It later merged with other institutions to form Jadavpur University.
 
• The college was a response to the partition of Bengal by the British, which was seen as an attempt to divide and weaken Indian nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement**
 
 
• A part of the Indian independence movement that emphasized self-sufficiency and the boycott of British goods.
 
• Led to the establishment of various national institutions, including educational ones, that aimed to reduce dependence on British systems.
 
 
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose**
 
 
• Born on 15 August 1872 and passed away on 5 December 1950.
 
• After his political career, he moved to Pondicherry and became a spiritual reformer, developing Integral Yoga.
 
• He authored several important texts, including "The Life Divine" and "Savitri."
 
 
 
• **Indian Freedom Struggle**
 
 
• The movement aimed at ending British colonial rule in India, spanning from the mid-19th century to 1947.
 
• Included various strategies such as non-violent resistance, civil disobedience, and armed struggle.
 
• Key figures included Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose, and many others.
